name: lodash-invoke-renamed-azul-transaction
behavioral_change: lodash v4.0.0 renamed `_.invoke` to `_.invokeMap` and reassigned the name `_.invoke` to a different function. In v_old, `_.invoke(collection, methodName)` called the named method on every element and returned an array of results; in v_new, `_.invoke(object, path, args)` calls the method at one path of an object and returns a single result.
downstream_effect: The downstream project calls `_.invoke(match[1].split(','), 'trim')` in index.js:223 to trim parsed parameter names; under v_new the call looks for a `trim` method on the whole array, silently returns undefined, and a later read of `params.length` throws `TypeError: Cannot read property 'length' of undefined`. The 17 failures never mention `invoke` or `invokeMap`; the stack frames name index.js and the function `route` but with istanbul-instrumented column numbers, and the throw site (index.js:236) is a different statement from the one that must be edited (index.js:223).
reference_fix: The reference fix replaces `_.invoke(match[1].split(','), 'trim')` with `_.invokeMap(match[1].split(','), 'trim')` in index.js:223.
documented_in: The lodash Changelog for v4.0.0 (https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki/Changelog), Compatibility Warnings section, "Method renames" list, states "Renamed `_.invoke` to `_.invokeMap`"; the entry has no accompanying code block, and the API reference for `_.invokeMap` (https://lodash.com/docs/4.17.21#invokeMap) describes the v_old semantics.
